name: Premenstrual dysphoric disorder
summary: Severe, cyclical mood symptoms (irritability, depressed mood, anxiety, affective lability) in the luteal phase that remit shortly after menses onset and cause marked impairment; diagnosis requires prospective daily ratings over at least two cycles. FDA-approved options are three serotonergic antidepressants (fluoxetine, sertraline, paroxetine controlled-release) and drospirenone/ethinyl estradiol 3 mg/0.02 mg oral contraceptives for those who choose an oral contraceptive. No new PMDD approvals were found for 2024 to 2026.
plainSummary: PMDD is a condition where mood symptoms like irritability, sadness, or anxiety become severe in the week or two before a period and get better once the period starts. Certain antidepressants and some birth control pills can help.

brands: Fluoxetine tablets 10 mg/20 mg (Torrent, PMDD-labeled generic)
approved.indication: Treatment of premenstrual dysphoric disorder (PMDD). Effectiveness beyond 6 months has not been systematically evaluated in placebo-controlled trials.

dosing.target: 20 mg/day, continuously (every day) or intermittently (start 14 days before expected menses through the first full day of menses, each cycle)
dosing.max: 80 mg/day (doses above 60 mg/day not studied in PMDD; 60 mg/day showed no added benefit over 20 mg/day)
dosing.notes: Use a lower or less frequent dose in hepatic impairment. Long half-life: allow 5 weeks after stopping before starting an MAOI or thioridazine.

boxedWarnings: Suicidal thoughts and behaviors in children, adolescents, and young adults
contraindications: MAOIs for psychiatric disorders (concurrently, within 5 weeks after stopping fluoxetine, or within 14 days after stopping the MAOI); linezolid or IV methylene blue
Thioridazine (including within 5 weeks after stopping fluoxetine)
approved.plainSummary: Fluoxetine is an antidepressant that can ease PMDD symptoms when taken every day or only in the two weeks before a period.

verified.note: Label text (effective 2024-12) checked for indication, dosing, boxed warning, and contraindications. Brand Sarafem is gone: FDA withdrew Sarafem capsules (NDA 018936) effective April 22, 2024 (Federal Register 2024-05982), and Sarafem tablets (NDA 021860) are listed as discontinued in Drugs@FDA. Searching all ~245 fluoxetine SPLs on DailyMed found only this Torrent fluoxetine tablet label carrying PMDD; Prozac and generic fluoxetine capsules/tablets referencing Prozac do not list PMDD. Prescribers should know that PMDD labeling depends on the specific product, though fluoxetine 20 mg is the same molecule. Approval year (2000, Sarafem) comes from secondary sources.

dosing.notes: Continuous: increase by 50 mg per menstrual cycle as needed. Intermittent: start 14 days before expected menses through onset of menses; if needed, use 50 mg/day for the first 3 days then 100 mg/day for the rest of each luteal-phase course. Mild hepatic impairment: halve the dose; moderate or severe hepatic impairment: not recommended. Oral solution must be diluted and is contraindicated with disulfiram.

boxedWarnings: Suicidal thoughts and behaviors in children, adolescents, and young adults
contraindications: MAOIs, including linezolid and IV methylene blue (concurrently or within 14 days)
approved.plainSummary: Sertraline is an antidepressant that can be taken daily or only in the two weeks before a period to reduce PMDD symptoms.

source.label: DailyMed: Zoloft (sertraline) tablets and oral solution prescribing information

verified.note: Indication, PMDD dosing (continuous and luteal-phase), boxed warning, and contraindications confirmed on the current Zoloft label. Approval year (2002) comes from secondary sources.

approved.indication: Treatment of premenstrual dysphoric disorder (PMDD) in adults. (Only the controlled-release formulation carries PMDD; immediate-release paroxetine does not.)

dosing.start: 12.5 mg once daily in the morning (continuous or luteal phase only)
dosing.notes: May increase by 12.5 mg/day at weekly intervals. Luteal-phase dosing starts 14 days before expected menses and continues through onset of menses. Same 25 mg/day maximum in patients 65 and older and in severe renal or hepatic impairment. Swallow whole; do not chew or crush. Taper when stopping.

boxedWarnings: Suicidal thoughts and behaviors in children, adolescents, and young adults
contraindications: MAOIs, including linezolid and IV methylene blue (concurrently or within 14 days)
Drugs that prolong the QTc interval and are CYP2D6 substrates
Hypersensitivity to paroxetine or inactive ingredients
approved.plainSummary: Paroxetine CR is a once-daily, slow-release antidepressant that can reduce PMDD symptoms when taken every day or just before periods.

source.label: DailyMed: Paxil CR (paroxetine) extended-release tablets prescribing information (Apotex)

verified.note: Indication, PMDD dosing, boxed warning, and contraindications confirmed on the Paxil CR label (effective 2026-09-30). The current label's contraindications list 'drugs that prolong QTc and are CYP2D6 substrates' and no longer names thioridazine/pimozide separately. Generic paroxetine ER tablets are on DailyMed. Approval year (2003) comes from secondary sources.

approved.generic: drospirenone 3 mg / ethinyl estradiol 0.02 mg (24/4 regimen)
approved.indication: Treatment of symptoms of PMDD in females of reproductive potential who choose to use an oral contraceptive as their method of contraception. Effectiveness for PMDD beyond 3 menstrual cycles has not been evaluated; not evaluated for premenstrual syndrome (PMS).

population.ages: Females of reproductive potential (postmenarchal; efficacy expected in postpubertal adolescents under 18)

dosing.start: 1 tablet daily (24 active tablets then 4 inert tablets per 28-day pack)
dosing.target: 1 tablet daily at the same time each day
dosing.notes: Day 1 or Sunday start; take in blister-pack order. Back-up contraception for the first 7 days if not started on Day 1. Drospirenone has antimineralocorticoid activity: check potassium in patients on drugs that raise potassium. Yasmin (3 mg/0.03 mg) is not PMDD-indicated.

formulations: Oral tablets (28-day blister pack: 24 active 3 mg DRSP/0.02 mg EE + 4 inert)
boxedWarnings: Cigarette smoking and serious cardiovascular events (do not use in women over 35 who smoke)
contraindications: High risk of arterial or venous thrombosis (e.g., smoker over 35, DVT/PE, cerebrovascular or coronary disease, thrombogenic valvular/rhythm disease, hypercoagulopathy, uncontrolled hypertension, diabetes with vascular disease, migraine with focal neurologic symptoms or migraine if over 35)
Hepatitis C regimens containing ombitasvir/paritaprevir/ritonavir, with or without dasabuvir
approved.plainSummary: Yaz is a birth control pill that can also ease PMDD symptoms for people who want to use the pill for birth control. It should not be used by smokers over 35.

source.label: DailyMed: Yaz (drospirenone/ethinyl estradiol) tablets prescribing information

verified.note: Indication (section 1.2), dosing, boxed warning, and contraindications confirmed on the Yaz label (effective 2025-05). Generic 3 mg/0.02 mg products Nikki (Lupin) and Vestura (Teva) confirmed to carry PMDD on DailyMed; other generics were not individually checked. Approval year (2006) comes from secondary sources.

approved.generic: drospirenone 3 mg / ethinyl estradiol 0.02 mg / levomefolate calcium 0.451 mg
approved.indication: Treatment of symptoms of PMDD in females of reproductive potential who choose to use an oral contraceptive as their method of contraception (also indicated to raise folate levels). Effectiveness for PMDD beyond 3 cycles not evaluated.

population.ages: Females of reproductive potential (postmenarchal; efficacy expected in postpubertal adolescents under 18)

dosing.start: 1 tablet daily (24 active tablets then 4 levomefolate-only tablets)
dosing.target: 1 tablet daily at the same time each day
dosing.notes: Same regimen and cautions as Yaz. Safyral and its generics (3 mg/0.03 mg with folate) are not PMDD-indicated.

formulations: Oral tablets (28-day blister pack: 24 active DRSP/EE/levomefolate + 4 levomefolate calcium 0.451 mg)
boxedWarnings: Cigarette smoking and serious cardiovascular events (do not use in women over 35 who smoke)
contraindications: High risk of arterial or venous thrombosis
Hepatitis C regimens containing ombitasvir/paritaprevir/ritonavir, with or without dasabuvir
approved.plainSummary: Beyaz is a birth control pill with added folate that can also ease PMDD symptoms for people who want to use the pill for birth control.

source.label: DailyMed: Beyaz (drospirenone/ethinyl estradiol/levomefolate calcium) prescribing information

verified.note: PMDD indication, dosing (1 tablet daily in pack order, Day 1 or Sunday start), strengths, boxed warning, and contraindications confirmed on the Beyaz label (effective 2026-03). Drugs@FDA lists NDA 022532 (approved 2010-09-24) as still marketed; approval year is the original NDA approval, and it was not separately confirmed that PMDD was part of that first approval. A generic (DailyMed setid 48f4301c-0426-43cd-af37-c4d8fc7aeb67) also carries PMDD.

offLabel.use: Continuous or luteal-phase treatment of PMDD
offLabel.notes: ACOG Clinical Practice Guideline No. 7 (2023) recommends SSRIs as a class (continuous or intermittent) for affective premenstrual symptoms. The 2024 Cochrane review found SSRIs effective for PMS/PMDD, with continuous dosing possibly more effective than intermittent. Common adverse effects include nausea, fatigue, and sexual dysfunction. Antidepressant boxed warning applies to adolescents and young adults.

details.labeledFor: Escitalopram and citalopram are FDA-approved for depression (and, for escitalopram, GAD); not for PMDD.

dosing.start: Escitalopram 5–10 mg or citalopram 10–20 mg daily (continuous, or from ovulation to menses onset)
dosing.notes: Luteal-phase dosing starts about 14 days before expected menses.

boxedWarnings: Suicidal thoughts and behaviors in children, adolescents, and young adults
warnings: Early activation or anxiety, GI upset, sexual dysfunction
Hyponatremia and bleeding risk (higher with NSAIDs/anticoagulants)
Serotonin syndrome with other serotonergic drugs
details.plainSummary: SSRIs other than the three approved ones are also widely used for PMDD, taken every day or only in the two weeks before a period.

references.label: ACOG Clinical Practice Guideline No. 7: Management of Premenstrual Disorders (2023)
Jespersen et al. SSRIs for PMS and PMDD. Cochrane 2024, PubMed

offLabel.use: PMDD when SSRIs are not tolerated or not effective
offLabel.notes: A placebo-controlled RCT (Freeman 2001, n=164, 50–200 mg/day) showed benefit. Watch for blood pressure increases, discontinuation symptoms with intermittent dosing, and the antidepressant boxed warning.

details.labeledFor: FDA-approved for depression, GAD, social anxiety, and panic disorder; not for PMDD.

dosing.notes: Check blood pressure; taper rather than stop abruptly.

boxedWarnings: Suicidal thoughts and behaviors in children, adolescents, and young adults
contraindications: MAOI use within 14 days (or linezolid / IV methylene blue)
details.plainSummary: An SNRI that worked in a trial for PMDD when SSRIs are not tolerated or do not help.

references.label: Freeman et al. Venlafaxine in the treatment of PMDD. Obstet Gynecol 2001, PubMed

offLabel.agent: GnRH agonists (e.g., leuprolide) with estrogen/progestin add-back
offLabel.notes: ACOG suggests GnRH agonists with combined hormonal add-back for adults with severe symptoms; not suggested for adolescents. Risks: hypoestrogenic effects (vasomotor symptoms, bone density loss), cost; add-back hormones can sometimes bring symptoms back. Usually managed with gynecology.

details.labeledFor: Leuprolide is FDA-approved for prostate cancer, endometriosis, fibroids, and central precocious puberty; no GnRH agonist is approved for PMDD.

dosing.start: Leuprolide depot 3.75 mg IM monthly, with add-back estrogen/progestogen to limit bone loss
dosing.target: Monthly dosing for a few months, reassessed
dosing.max: Limit duration; monitor bone density (often for 6 months or less without add-back)
dosing.notes: Coordinate with gynecology; not suggested for adolescents.

formulations: Add-back: transdermal or oral estradiol with a progestogen
warnings: Menopausal symptoms and bone density loss
Add-back hormones can bring symptoms back
details.plainSummary: A hormone-blocking treatment for very severe PMDD that does not respond to other options. Doctors add back small hormone doses to protect the bones.

references.label: ACOG Clinical Practice Guideline No. 7: Management of Premenstrual Disorders (2023)
AAFP summary of ACOG premenstrual disorders guideline (2024)

offLabel.agent: Other combined hormonal contraceptives (including continuous or extended-cycle regimens)
offLabel.use: PMDD symptoms in patients who also want contraception
offLabel.notes: ACOG notes COCs moderately improve premenstrual symptoms other than depressive symptoms. Only drospirenone 3 mg/EE 0.02 mg products carry PMDD labeling. Mood may worsen with some progestins. Usual COC thrombosis and smoking cautions apply.

details.labeledFor: Only drospirenone 3 mg/ethinyl estradiol 20 mcg products are FDA-labeled for PMDD; other combined contraceptives are not.

dosing.start: One active pill daily (extended or continuous regimens skip the inactive pills)
dosing.target: Same pill daily at the same time
dosing.notes: Mood can worsen with some progestins.

formulations: Combined oral contraceptive tablets, patches, vaginal rings
boxedWarnings: Cigarette smoking and serious cardiovascular events (women over 35 who smoke)
contraindications: History of thrombosis, stroke, or heart disease
Smoking over age 35; liver tumors or disease
details.plainSummary: Birth-control pills other than the approved one may help some physical premenstrual symptoms and suit people who also want contraception.
